subject: general
question: If the cost price of 60 guavas is equal to the selling price of 45 guavas, what is the profit percentage (rounded off to 2 decimal places)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP of 60 = SP of 45

⇒ SP/CP = 60/45 = 4/3

Profit = (4/3 − 1) = 1/3

Profit% = (1/3) × 100 = 33.33%

**∴ Answer = 33.33% gain**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

CP of 60 guavas = SP of 45 guavas

**Formula used:**

Profit % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP of 1 guava = 1

⇒ CP of 60 guavas = 60

⇒ SP of 45 guavas = 60

⇒ SP of 1 guava = 60 ÷ 45 = 4/3

⇒ Profit per guava = 4/3 − 1 = 1/3

⇒ Profit % = (1/3) × 100 = 33.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Method

Convert total CP and SP into per unit values.

Profit Formula

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Ratio Insight

If SP/CP > 1 ⇒ profit, if < 1 ⇒ loss.
